column3: MT 49:1–2; the following verses of this psalm are MT +1. NASB sets the title in braces before verse 1. Close to the Hebrew.
“Children of humankind and children of man” is rendered “low and high.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew; “I will open my riddle” is rendered “I will express my riddle.”
“The iniquity of my heels” is rendered “the iniquity of my foes.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew; “a brother no one can ransom” is rendered “No man can by any means redeem his brother.”
Close to the Hebrew; “their life” is rendered “his soul,” and NASB supplies “trying.”
Close to the Hebrew; “see the pit” is rendered “undergo decay.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB supplies “even.”
The Hebrew reads “their inward part (is) their houses”; NASB renders “Their inner thought is, that their houses are forever.” The meaning is uncertain.
“In honor” is rendered “in his pomp,” and “does not lodge” as “will not endure.”
“They delight in their mouth” is rendered “who approve their words.”
The Hebrew end is obscure (“from His lofty abode”); NASB renders “So that they have no habitation.” The meaning is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew; “will take me” is rendered “will receive me.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
“He blessed his soul” is rendered “he congratulates himself.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew; “in honor” is rendered “in his pomp.”
